scope.excluded: Other kernels or boards, runtime call reachability, benchmark execution, general alias/type inference, macro expansion, ABI proof and safety scoring.

identifiers.c_enum_value: Numerical value derived from the ordered C enum declaration, not a wire ID.
identifiers.c_wire_id: Protocol case ID produced by sink_case_id in bench.c and accepted by s_case_map.
identifiers.rust_discriminant: Numerical discriminant derived from the ordered Rust enum declaration, not a wire ID.
identifiers.rust_wire_id: Protocol ID produced by case_id_for and accepted by rust_bench_run_case.
identifiers.note: Thesis numbers, C enumerators, C enum values, Rust variants, Rust discriminants and wire IDs are separate identifier spaces.

target_categories.rtos_api: A resolved external FreeRTOS API target. This is the only category counted as an underlying RTOS API target.
target_categories.c_bridge_definition: A project-written C function under RUST=1 that is invoked through Rust FFI. It is a bridge, not an RTOS API.
target_categories.matched_rtos_api: A per-mechanism RTOS API target reached by both C and Rust evidence.
target_categories.matched_c_bridge_definition: A selected C bridge definition with a Rust FFI call and a resolved C definition.
target_categories.unused_c_bridge_definition: A configured C bridge definition with no selected Rust FFI call and no resolved C-to-bridge call. Its body is not traversed.
target_categories.unresolved_rtos_target: A target that cannot be established from supported source evidence.
target_categories.c_only_rtos_api: An RTOS API reached from the C side but not from Rust evidence.
target_categories.rust_only_rtos_api: An RTOS API reached from Rust evidence but not from C evidence.

levels.A: Application-facing interface: calls written in shared benchmark sequencing or application code.
levels.B: Project-written implementation and adaptation: C adapters, C bridges, C ISR/callback bodies, Rust wrappers and Rust callback bodies.
levels.C: Underlying external RTOS API boundary: the actual FreeRTOS call and its arguments, independent of whether it is reached from C, Rust FFI or a C bridge.
levels.membership: Levels are properties, not one mutually exclusive label. A C adapter RTOS call and a Rust wrapper FFI RTOS call are members of Level B and Level C.

views.mechanism_specific: Calls and checks associated with the selected mechanism rather than the shared harness.
views.common_harness: Calls in shared benchmark sequencing, including the two now_ticks calls and shared dispatch checks.
views.combined: Mechanism-specific and common-harness membership. Shared source occurrences are still counted once in distinct-source totals.
views.case_comparison: Per-case values are memberships unless the field name explicitly says occurrences; size fields are split by language and level.

definitions.configuration_specific_call_site: One call expression identified by configuration, language, caller, source file, line, column, invocation name and resolved target.
definitions.distinct_source_call_site: The same source location and target ignoring build configuration. Used to avoid calling duplicated C configurations distinct source operations.
definitions.per_case_membership: A call site associated with a benchmark mechanism. One source occurrence can have several memberships.
definitions.application_facing_interface: The C bench_port method or Rust Port method called by shared benchmark sequencing.
definitions.reachable_bridge: A C bridge definition reached by a selected Rust FFI call or by a resolved C call on the selected path.
definitions.unused_bridge: A configured bridge definition with no mechanically established reachability. It remains in the bridge inventory and is not traversed.
definitions.callback_registration: A function item or function pointer passed to a supported task-creation API. It is not an ordinary synchronous call edge.
definitions.callback_body_path: Operations reached by traversing a uniquely resolved callback definition. It is labelled as external-entry evidence and does not prove runtime execution.
definitions.raw_pointer_argument: An argument whose resolved parameter is pointer-typed or whose source expression is an address or pointer conversion. Includes handles and dispatch context unless separated by role.
definitions.raw_data_pointer_argument: An output, buffer or other data pointer. Dispatch context pointers and resource handles are reported separately.
definitions.dispatch_context_argument: The generic C port context pointer such as port->ctx.
definitions.output_pointer_argument: A pointer used to return a value, such as an elapsed-ticks or received-payload output.
definitions.buffer_pointer_argument: A pointer to a payload, buffer, item or block.
definitions.resource_handle_argument: A pointer-typed or declared RTOS handle such as QueueHandle_t.
definitions.function_pointer_callback_argument: A function-pointer or explicit callback argument.
definitions.explicit_size_argument: A size, length, capacity or depth parameter whose source value is supplied separately.
definitions.derived_size_argument: A size argument derived from sizeof, size_of, a supported length expression or a documented constant-size derivation.
definitions.observed_check: An if/match/while condition or comparison expression present in a selected path. It is a source pattern, not proof of contract enforcement.
definitions.unsafe_context_membership: A Rust call lexically inside an active unsafe block or unsafe function. It is not an intrinsically unsafe-call count.

rules.root_matching: Verify thesis names, C enumerators and values, wire maps, Rust variants and discriminants, dispatchers, C port initializer and Rust impl methods from source. A case is verified only when the checks agree.
rules.c_call_resolution: Use libclang referenced declarations for direct calls. For function-like macros record the source invocation and the resolved expansion target separately; they are one application call.
rules.c_indirect_calls: Resolve bench_port function-pointer members only through the verified initializer map. Other indirect calls remain unresolved.
rules.rust_call_resolution: Use syn direct calls, method calls, foreign declarations and qualified names. Resolve only unambiguous targets; aliases, generics, function variables and unsupported non-self methods remain unresolved.
rules.ffi_mapping: Match Rust foreign names exactly to C declarations or definitions. Project definitions take precedence. Multiple incompatible candidates are ambiguous. Matching names do not prove ABI or behaviour.
rules.bridge_reachability: Traverse a C bridge only if a selected Rust FFI call or a resolved C call reaches it. Do not treat every configured bridge root as reachable. Keep unused definitions in the bridge inventory.
rules.bridge_relationship: A bridge row records the C definition and the Rust FFI call. Calls inside the bridge are not calls to the bridge; they are Level B bridge-body operations and may contribute Level C RTOS targets.
rules.shared_c_isr: Case 16 uses the C TIM2_IRQHandler as an explicit external root. Its RTOS calls are cross-language Rust-path evidence only when the Rust adapter uses the same C ISR path; they are not Rust-language calls.
rules.argument_roles: Use resolved parameter type, parameter name, source expression and recognised syntactic form. A name prefix alone is insufficient for a handle. Callback parameters require function-pointer evidence. Unknown evidence remains unknown.
rules.derived_size: Set derived_size only when the argument role is a size and the expression follows sizeof, size_of, supported len() or a documented constant-size derivation. Array subscripts are not derived sizes.
rules.checks: Classify from the parsed condition shape (operator, operands, call flags and operand types). Do not classify NULL appearing inside a call argument as a null check. Distinguish pointer null, numeric zero, status, size/bound, temporal/ordering, boolean result and flag checks.
rules.return_handling: Preserve the outer value-use context through nested blocks. Distinguish returned/function-tail, stored/assigned, condition, propagated, used-as-argument, discarded and unresolved. Do not map every block tail to function return.
rules.exposure_levels: Attach role and level membership to the call occurrence. A call can be Level B implementation and Level C RTOS target. Do not assign a single global level to a function compiled in several configurations.
rules.checks_counting: Keep configuration-specific check occurrences, distinct source conditions and per-path memberships separate. Common dispatch checks do not become mechanism-specific by being called from every case.
rules.callbacks: Record registration, callback symbol, definition, invocation mechanism and resolution. A uniquely resolved callback body may be traversed as an external-entry path. Unresolved callbacks make coverage partial.
rules.shared_wrappers: Merge call-site identity by configuration/source/target and report per-case membership separately. Common harness calls are not duplicated into five distinct source operations.
rules.provenance: Record source revision, source hashes, tool versions and a canonical manifest. Canonical output contains relative repository paths only.

counting_units.call_site_occurrences: Unique configuration-specific call-site IDs after merging repeated case membership.
counting_units.configuration_specific_call_sites: Same as call_site_occurrences; the configuration is part of the ID.
counting_units.distinct_source_call_sites: Unique source occurrence ID ignoring configuration.
counting_units.per_case_call_memberships: Sum of case memberships across call-site occurrences.
counting_units.rtos_api_target_relationships: Per-case relationships to underlying RTOS API targets.
counting_units.distinct_rtos_api_targets: Unique underlying RTOS API names across the five cases.
counting_units.argument_rows: Per-call argument occurrences after case merging.
counting_units.distinct_source_checks: Distinct source conditions ignoring configuration and case membership (432).
counting_units.unsafe_context_call_sites: Rust call edges lexically inside an active Stage 1 unsafe context.
counting_units.callback_registrations: Per-case callback registrations on selected paths.
counting_units.case_canonical_call_site: One row per configuration-specific call-site identity in call-sites.csv.
counting_units.case_membership: One row per call-site/benchmark-case relation in case-memberships.csv; summation is the per-case membership count.
counting_units.distinct_source: Unique source occurrence ignoring configuration; not a per-case membership count.
counting_units.rtos_relationship: One per-case underlying RTOS API relationship; bridge rows are not included.
counting_units.bridge_relationship: One per-case project C bridge definition relationship; distinct bridge names are counted separately.
counting_units.argument: One per call-site argument occurrence; per-case membership is supplied by cases.
counting_units.check: Configuration-specific observed condition; distinct source checks are counted separately.
counting_units.selected_c_bridge_relationships: Per-case relationship to a selected/configured/reached project C bridge definition (71 in the 26-case run).
counting_units.selected_distinct_c_bridge_definitions: Unique selected/configured/reached project C bridge names (45). This is not an inventory of every C-support function compiled under RUST=1.
counting_units.selected_matched_c_bridge_relationships: Per-case selected bridge relationships with a Rust FFI call and C definition (70).
counting_units.selected_unused_c_bridge_definitions: Selected configured bridges with no established Rust/C reachability (1, bench_frag_measure).
counting_units.c_bridge_inventory_scope: selected/configured/reached Stage 2 bridge definitions; unselected C-support functions are outside this inventory.
counting_units.c_all_level_explicit_size_occurrences: Distinct C explicit-size argument occurrences at any exposure level (46).
counting_units.rust_all_level_explicit_size_occurrences: Distinct Rust explicit-size argument occurrences at any exposure level (30).
counting_units.c_all_level_explicit_size_memberships: C explicit-size argument memberships across cases at any level (48).
counting_units.rust_all_level_explicit_size_memberships: Rust explicit-size argument memberships across cases at any level (47).
counting_units.c_all_level_derived_size_occurrences: Distinct C derived-size argument occurrences at any level (5).
counting_units.rust_all_level_derived_size_occurrences: Distinct Rust derived-size argument occurrences at any level (1).
counting_units.c_application_explicit_size_occurrences: Distinct C Level A explicit-size argument occurrences (2).
counting_units.rust_application_explicit_size_occurrenc: Distinct Rust Level A explicit-size argument occurrences (3).
counting_units.c_application_explicit_size_memberships: C Level A explicit-size argument memberships (2).
counting_units.rust_application_explicit_size_membershi: Rust Level A explicit-size argument memberships (3).
counting_units.c_application_derived_size_occurrences: Distinct C Level A derived-size argument occurrences (0).
counting_units.rust_application_derived_size_occurrence: Distinct Rust Level A derived-size argument occurrences (0).
counting_units.c_application_derived_size_memberships: C Level A derived-size argument memberships (0).
counting_units.rust_application_derived_size_membership: Rust Level A derived-size argument memberships (0).
counting_units.unsafe_context_call_occurrences: Canonical Rust call-site occurrences lexically inside an active unsafe context (250).
counting_units.unsafe_context_per_case_memberships: Per-case memberships of those unsafe-context calls (288).
counting_units.unsafe_context_distinct_source_identitie: Distinct source identities among unsafe-context calls (250).
counting_units.common_harness_check_memberships: Per-case memberships of common-harness checks (1014; function-scope shared sample conditions).

supported_with_qualification: direct C/Rust path segments within the declared parser model
underlying RTOS API target names reached by each side
project C bridge definitions and their Rust FFI calls
application-facing argument roles for validated source patterns
observed check expressions by source condition and configuration
descriptive_only: callback-body operations without runtime scheduling evidence
operation counts on a source path
shared-C ISR operations for the Rust benchmark
FFI source-signature pairings without ABI proof
not_established: defect frequency or a safety score

case_coverage.rule: A case with an unsupported external entry, unresolved callback, unresolved root or unresolved selected edge is partial; it remains in every result table.

reproducibility.note: Two independent runs must be byte-identical; canonical output contains relative paths only. The five-case profile preserves the validated Phase A regression baseline.

size_reporting.rule: Size fields are split by language, exposure level and counting unit. Level A is application-facing; all-level means membership in any of A/B/C and is not a C-only or application-only total.
size_reporting.warning: Do not label 95 per-case or 76 unique explicit-size values as C application-facing. Those are all-level, both-language memberships/occurrences. Level A is C 2/Rust 3 explicit and 0 derived.

check_reporting.distinction: Check occurrences, distinct source checks, common-harness occurrences, mechanism-specific occurrences and per-case memberships are separate units.
common_harness: Source conditions in shared benchmark sequencing.
They are not necessarily executed or relevant in every case.
They are not automatically API argument preconditions or safety guarantees.
Use mechanism-specific checks for per-case API observations.
Presence or absence of a recognised check does not prove correctness.
check_reporting.unsafe: 250 is lexical Rust unsafe-context call membership; it is not an intrinsic-unsafety count, distinct-block count, ABI proof or vulnerability count.

bridge_reporting.scope: The C bridge counts cover selected/configured/reached Stage 2 bridge definitions only. They do not enumerate every C-support function compiled under RUST=1.
bridge_reporting.rule: Unselected C-support functions are not reached paths and are not added to the bridge inventory. bench_frag_measure remains the configured unused bridge.
